# docker Provider

The `docker` provider manages the whole Docker chain, from image builds to Swarm stacks, through the Docker Engine
API. It never runs the `docker` CLI or the compose plugin: compose files are parsed in-process by `docker_compose`,
SSH hosts are reached in pure Go, and the only external program it can start is a docker credential helper, and only
with `allow_credential_helpers = true` (see [Registry credentials](#registry-credentials)).

Types fall into four layers. Create them in this order; destroy runs in reverse.

| Layer | Resources | Data sources |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Image | `docker_image`, `docker_tag`, `docker_registry_image`, `docker_buildx_builder` | `docker_image`, `docker_registry_image` |
| 2. Single host | `docker_network`, `docker_volume`, `docker_container`, `docker_plugin`, `docker_compose` (local mode) | `docker_network`, `docker_volume`, `docker_container` |
| 3. Swarm topology | `docker_swarm_init`, `docker_swarm_node` | `docker_swarm_tokens`, `docker_node`, `docker_nodes` |
| 4. Swarm workload | `docker_secret`, `docker_config`, `docker_service`, `docker_stack`, `docker_compose` (swarm mode) | `docker_secret`, `docker_config`, `docker_service`, `docker_stack` |

`docker_swarm_init` must exist before overlay networks, secrets, configs and services; `docker_swarm_node` joins
further hosts with the tokens `docker_swarm_init` exports.

Actions and list resources need Terraform >= 1.14, write-only `*_wo` arguments >= 1.11, and ephemeral resources
>= 1.10.

`docker_buildx_builder` with `driver = "cloud"` (Docker Build Cloud) is implemented but not yet verified against the
live Build Cloud service.

## Connecting to the daemon

The endpoint is chosen in this order: `host`; the `ssh` block's `host`; `context`; `DOCKER_HOST`; `DOCKER_CONTEXT`;
`currentContext` in the docker `config.json` (under `DOCKER_CONFIG`, default `~/.docker`); and finally
`unix:///var/run/docker.sock`. The context named `default` means "no context".

- **Docker contexts.** `context = "staging"` reads the context store written by `docker context create`, through
  docker/cli's context store package. The context supplies the host, its TLS material and `skip-tls-verify`. An
  `ssh://` context host uses the SSH transport below.
- **TLS.** Give the `tls` block (PEM content or paths), or `cert_path`, a directory holding `ca.pem`, `cert.pem` and
  `key.pem`. You can't set both; plan rejects that. With neither set, TLS material comes from the context, or from
  `DOCKER_CERT_PATH` when `DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY` is set.
- **SSH.** An `ssh://user@host[:port]` host, or an `ssh` block, reaches the daemon over SSH in pure Go
  (golang.org/x/crypto/ssh). No `ssh` binary runs. The provider opens one connection per distinct configuration,
  reuses it for every API call, and opens a `direct-streamlocal@openssh.com` channel to `remote_socket` for each one.
  Authentication can use `identity_file`, the SSH agent (`identity_agent`: `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, or the Windows OpenSSH
  agent pipe) and `password` / `password_wo`. Host keys are checked against `known_hosts_file` unless
  `strict_host_key_checking = false`. `proxy_jump` chains through one or more bastions. `docker_swarm_node` takes the
  same `ssh` block for each joining node.
- **Daemon check.** Configure pings the daemon once. If the daemon doesn't answer, you get a *warning* that says why
  (not reachable, permission denied on the socket or pipe, or a TLS failure): validate and plan never fail because a
  daemon is missing. Set `disable_docker_daemon_check = true` to skip the ping. Either way, the client makes no other
  call until a resource or data source needs the daemon.

## Engine API floor: `min_api_version`

`min_api_version` is the oldest Docker Engine API version the provider accepts, in the form `1.NN`. The default is
`1.44` (Docker Engine 25.0). It cannot be above the newest version the provider speaks.

- When Configure pings the daemon and the negotiated version is older, configuration fails with an error naming both
  versions. With `disable_docker_daemon_check = true`, or when the daemon could not be reached at plan time, the same
  error comes from the first operation that asks for the version.
- A pinned `api_version` below `min_api_version` is rejected.
- There is no environment variable for it: the docker CLI has no API floor setting to mirror.

## Registry credentials

For one registry, credentials come from the first of these that matches:

| # | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | A `registry_auth` block for the registry: `username` with `password` (or `password_wo`) | |
| 2 | The same block: `DOCKER_REGISTRY_USER` / `DOCKER_REGISTRY_PASS` | Only when the block names no config file. |
| 3 | The same block: its docker config (`config_file_content`, else `config_file`, else the default config) | Looked up as below. A block that resolves to nothing is an error. |
| 4 | No block: the default docker config (`DOCKER_CONFIG`, a directory or a file, else `~/.docker/config.json`) | Read on first use and cached per registry. Nothing found means anonymous, never an error. |
| 5 | Anonymous | |

Inside a docker config the order is the docker CLI's: `credHelpers[<registry>]`, then `credsStore`, then `auths`.

- `credHelpers` and `credsStore` both run a `docker-credential-<name>` helper found on `PATH`. That is the provider's
  only exception to "nothing shells out", and it needs `allow_credential_helpers = true` (default `false`).
- A helper that answers "credentials not found", fails, or is not allowed falls back to the `auths` entry for the
  registry when there is one. A registry whose credentials live only in a disallowed helper gives an error that names
  the setting.
- Docker Hub is looked up under `https://index.docker.io/v1/`, other registries under their bare `host[:port]`.
- `auth_disabled = true` on a block makes that registry anonymous.

The provider's own registry reads (`docker_registry_image` delete, the registry data sources and the
`docker_registry_token` ephemeral resource) use the same resolution.

## Owner labels

Set `owner` and every object the provider creates carries the label `io.terraform.provider.owner=<owner>`. Unset (the
default), nothing is labelled and nothing is checked.

- **Resources** (`docker_container`, `docker_network`, `docker_volume`, `docker_image` builds,
  `docker_buildx_builder`, `docker_secret`, `docker_config`, `docker_service`, `docker_stack`, `docker_swarm_init`,
  `docker_swarm_node`, `docker_compose`) add the label, and create fails with an error naming both owners when an
  object of the same name already carries a different owner label. Managing such an object (after `terraform
  import`, for example) needs `adopt = true` on the resource; without it the plan fails. The label is kept out of the
  `labels` attribute, so it never shows as drift.
- **Actions** that create objects (`docker_container_run`, `docker_image_commit`, `docker_image_import`,
  `docker_compose_run`, `docker_buildx_bake`, `docker_compose_build`, `docker_compose_commit`,
  `docker_compose_scale`) add the label for forensics only: an action owns nothing in state, so it runs no conflict
  check and takes no `adopt`.
- **No label**, by design: `docker_image_load` (images load exactly as saved), `docker_node` (manages an existing
  node), `docker_plugin` and `docker_plugin_create` (plugins have no labels), `docker_tag`, `docker_registry_image` and
  `docker_registry_manifest_list` (registry objects carry no Docker labels).

## Outputs for downstream consumers

Every resource and data source exposes its full result as computed attributes, so another module or provider can
consume one field or the whole object. On `docker_container`, `docker_service`, `docker_network` and `docker_volume`:

| Attribute | What it is | Changes when |
|---|---|---|
| `inspect` | The Engine API inspect response as a nested object, field by field in snake_case (`inspect.state.status`, `inspect.host_config.memory`). | Anything in the inspect response changes. |
| `inspect_json` | The inspect response body exactly as the Engine returned it (surrounding whitespace trimmed). Sensitive where a secret channel (env, driver options) can reach it. | Anything in the inspect response changes. |
| `content_sha256` | sha256 of `inspect_json`. | Anything changes, including runtime state: a restart, a new IP, a health check result, a task update. |
| `config_sha256` | sha256 of the configuration part of the inspect response only. | The object's configuration changes. Runtime state does not move it. |

Watch `config_sha256` to trigger downstream work (a `terraform_data` replacement, a config-management run) on a real
configuration change; `content_sha256` also moves on every restart or state change. Sensitivity is per field: only
fields a secret can reach (env, driver options, build args, tokens) are marked, so image names, ports and labels stay
readable in plans. Version outputs (`engine_api_version`, `docker_server_version`) say which daemon produced the
result.

- [Migrating from kreuzwerker/docker](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/JerryBalmer1/docker/latest/docs/guides/migrating-from-kreuzwerker):

A generated agent skill with the dependency rules, the attributes that force replacement and a worked cold-start

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.14.0"

  required_providers {
    docker = {
      source = "JerryBalmer1/docker"
    }
  }
}

# Local daemon: DOCKER_HOST, else the current Docker CLI context, else
# unix:///var/run/docker.sock.
provider "docker" {}

# Remote daemon over TLS with registry credentials.
provider "docker" {
  alias = "remote"
  host  = "tcp://10.0.0.5:2376"

  tls {
    ca   = "~/.docker/remote/ca.pem"
    cert = "~/.docker/remote/cert.pem"
    key  = "~/.docker/remote/key.pem"
  }

  registry_auth {
    address  = "ghcr.io"
    username = "octocat"
    password = var.ghcr_token
  }
}

# The same TLS host with cert_path: a directory holding ca.pem, cert.pem and
# key.pem. cert_path and the tls block are mutually exclusive.
provider "docker" {
  alias     = "remote_certs"
  host      = "tcp://10.0.0.5:2376"
  cert_path = "~/.docker/remote"
}

# A Docker CLI context created with `docker context create staging ...`.
# Host and TLS material come from ~/.docker/contexts (or DOCKER_CONFIG).
provider "docker" {
  alias   = "staging"
  context = "staging"
}

# SSH in pure Go (no ssh binary): one connection, reused for every call and
# forwarded to the remote daemon's unix socket, here through a bastion.
provider "docker" {
  alias = "ssh"
  host  = "ssh://deploy@10.0.1.20"

  ssh {
    identity_file    = "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"
    identity_agent   = true
    known_hosts_file = "~/.ssh/known_hosts"
    proxy_jump       = "deploy@bastion.example.com:22"
    connect_timeout  = "15s"
    remote_socket    = "/var/run/docker.sock"
  }

  # Skip the plan-time ping (it only ever warns) when the host may be down.
  disable_docker_daemon_check = true
}

# Registry credentials from docker config.json files, including credsStore /
# credHelpers (Docker Desktop's "desktop" helper, ecr-login, ...). Running
# docker-credential-* helpers must be allowed explicitly.
provider "docker" {
  alias                    = "helpers"
  allow_credential_helpers = true

  registry_auth {
    address     = "registry-1.docker.io"
    config_file = "~/.docker/config.json"
  }

  registry_auth {
    address             = "123456789012.dkr.ecr.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com"
    config_file_content = var.docker_config_json
  }

  registry_auth {
    address       = "public.ecr.aws"
    auth_disabled = true
  }
}

variable "ghcr_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "docker_config_json" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  default   = "{\"credHelpers\": {\"123456789012.dkr.ecr.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com\": \"ecr-login\"}}"
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `allow_credential_helpers` (Boolean) Let the provider run the docker credential helpers (`docker-credential-<name>`, found on `PATH`) named by `credHelpers` / `credsStore` in a docker `config.json`, for `registry_auth` blocks and for registries without one. The helper is called as `docker-credential-<name> get` with the registry on stdin and answers JSON (`ServerURL`, `Username`, `Secret`) on stdout; "credentials not found" falls back to `auths`. Default `false`: the provider never starts another program, a `registry_auth` block whose credentials only live in a helper is an error naming this attribute, and a registry without a block is accessed anonymously. This is the provider's one documented exception to running nothing external.
- `api_version` (String) Engine API version to pin, e.g. `1.47`. Environment: `DOCKER_API_VERSION`. Default: negotiated with the daemon.
- `cert_path` (String) Directory holding `ca.pem`, `cert.pem` and `key.pem` for a TLS `tcp://` host: a shortcut for the `tls` block, and mutually exclusive with it (checked at plan time). `~` expands to the home directory.
- `context` (String) Name of a Docker CLI context (as created by `docker context create`), read from `contexts/` under `DOCKER_CONFIG` (default `~/.docker`). It supplies the host, TLS material and `skip-tls-verify`; an `ssh://` context host uses the pure-Go `ssh` transport (the `ssh` block can add credentials). An explicitly set `host` wins. `default` means no context. Environment: `DOCKER_CONTEXT` (applies only when `DOCKER_HOST` is unset), then `currentContext` in `config.json`.
- `disable_docker_daemon_check` (Boolean) Skip the daemon reachability check. When `false` (default), Configure pings the daemon (`GET /_ping`, 5s timeout, plus `ssh.connect_timeout` for SSH hosts) and reports a *warning* if it does not answer, classified as not reachable, permission denied (unix socket or named pipe) or TLS failure, naming the host, where it came from and the TLS settings in effect; it never fails validate or plan. A daemon below `min_api_version` is an error. The ping is skipped while a `tls` or `ssh` value is unknown until apply. The client itself is lazy either way: no other daemon call happens until a resource or data source needs one. Set `true` to skip the ping (no delay when the daemon is expected to be absent at plan time).
- `host` (String) Docker daemon address, e.g. `unix:///var/run/docker.sock`, `npipe:////./pipe/docker_engine`, `tcp://10.0.0.5:2376` or `ssh://user@10.0.0.5[:port]` (see the `ssh` block). Environment: `DOCKER_HOST`. Wins over `context`. Default: the Docker context, else `unix:///var/run/docker.sock`.
- `min_api_version` (String) Oldest Docker Engine API version the provider accepts from the daemon, in the form `1.NN`. Default: `1.44` (Docker Engine 25.0). It cannot be above `1.56`, the newest version this provider speaks. When Configure pings the daemon and the negotiated version is older, configuration fails with an error naming both versions; with `disable_docker_daemon_check = true` (or an unreachable daemon) the same error comes from the first operation that asks for the version. A pinned `api_version` below it is rejected. There is no environment variable: the docker CLI has no API floor setting to mirror.
- `owner` (String) Ownership label value. When set, every object the provider creates gets the label `io.terraform.provider.owner=<owner>`; creating an object whose name is taken by an object carrying a different owner label fails; and managing (for example importing) an object owned by someone else needs `adopt = true` on that resource. Unset (default): no labels and no checks.
- `registry_auth` (Block List) Credentials for registries, used for pulls and pushes. A registry without a block gets the default docker config's credentials (`DOCKER_CONFIG`, else `~/.docker/config.json`), or none. Sources in a block, first match wins: `username` with `password`/`password_wo`; `DOCKER_REGISTRY_USER`/`DOCKER_REGISTRY_PASS` (when no config file is named); `config_file_content`; `config_file`; the default config (`DOCKER_CONFIG`, a directory or a file, else `~/.docker/config.json`). In a config file, `credHelpers` and `credsStore` are honored like the docker CLI (needs `allow_credential_helpers`), falling back to `auths` entries. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--registry_auth))
- `ssh` (Block, Optional) Reach the Docker daemon over SSH in pure Go (no `ssh` binary is run): the provider opens one SSH connection, reuses it for every API call, and forwards each call to the remote daemon's unix socket. Applies when the Docker host is `ssh://user@host[:port]` (from `host`, the Docker context or `DOCKER_HOST`), or when `host` is unset and this block names a `host`. Provider configuration is never written to state, so `password` and `password_wo` behave the same here; `password_wo` exists for symmetry with resources. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--ssh))
- `tls` (Block, Optional) TLS client material for a `tcp://` host. Each value is PEM content or a path to a PEM file. Conflicts with `cert_path`. When neither is set, TLS material comes from the Docker context, else (with `DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY` set) `ca.pem`, `cert.pem` and `key.pem` are read from `DOCKER_CERT_PATH`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tls))

<a id="nestedblock--registry_auth"></a>
### Nested Schema for `registry_auth`

Required:

- `address` (String) Registry host, e.g. `registry-1.docker.io` or `ghcr.io`.

Optional:

- `auth_disabled` (Boolean) Access this registry anonymously: no credentials are looked up or sent. Default `false`.
- `config_file` (String) Path to a docker `config.json`. `~` expands to the home directory. Default: `DOCKER_CONFIG` (directory or file), else `~/.docker/config.json`. Conflicts with `config_file_content`.
- `config_file_content` (String, Sensitive) Content of a docker `config.json` (e.g. `file("~/.docker/config.json")` or a secret). Conflicts with `config_file`.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Registry password or token. Environment: `DOCKER_REGISTRY_PASS`. Conflicts with `password_wo`.
- `password_wo` (String, Sensitive) Registry password or token, the write-only spelling of `password` (conflicts with it). Provider configuration is never stored in state, so both are equally ephemeral here; Terraform's write-only marker only exists for resource schemas.
- `username` (String) Registry user. Environment: `DOCKER_REGISTRY_USER` (when no config file is named).


<a id="nestedblock--ssh"></a>
### Nested Schema for `ssh`

Optional:

- `connect_timeout` (String) Timeout for the TCP connection plus SSH handshake of each hop, as a Go duration (`10s`, `1m`). Default `10s`.
- `host` (String) SSH server host name or IP. Default: the host of an `ssh://` Docker host (from `host`, the Docker context or `DOCKER_HOST`).
- `identity_agent` (Boolean) Also offer the keys held by the running SSH agent: `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` on Linux/macOS, the Windows OpenSSH agent named pipe `\\.\pipe\openssh-ssh-agent` on Windows (or `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` when it names a pipe). Default `false`.
- `identity_file` (String, Sensitive) Private key used for public-key authentication: PEM/OpenSSH content or a path (`~` expands). Passphrase-protected keys are not supported; load them into an agent and use `identity_agent`. When unset, `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, `~/.ssh/id_ecdsa` and `~/.ssh/id_rsa` are offered if they exist and are unencrypted.
- `known_hosts_file` (String) OpenSSH `known_hosts` file used to verify the server's host key (and every `proxy_jump` hop). Default `~/.ssh/known_hosts`.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) SSH password (password and keyboard-interactive authentication). Conflicts with `password_wo`.
- `password_wo` (String, Sensitive) SSH password, write-only variant of `password`. Conflicts with `password`.
- `port` (Number) SSH server port. Default `22` (or the port in an `ssh://` Docker host).
- `proxy_jump` (String) Jump host(s) to reach the server through, OpenSSH `ProxyJump` style: `user@host:port`, or several hops separated by commas (`user@bastion:22,user@inner:2222`), dialled in order. User defaults to `user`, port to `22`. Each hop is authenticated with the same credentials and checked against the same `known_hosts_file`.
- `remote_socket` (String) Path of the Docker daemon's unix socket on the remote host. Default `/var/run/docker.sock`.
- `strict_host_key_checking` (Boolean) Reject servers whose host key is missing from, or does not match, `known_hosts_file`. Default `true`. `false` accepts any host key (insecure; for throwaway hosts only).
- `user` (String) SSH user. Default: the user in an `ssh://user@host` Docker host, else `USER`/`USERNAME` from the environment.


<a id="nestedblock--tls"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tls`

Optional:

- `ca` (String) CA certificate (PEM or path).
- `cert` (String) Client certificate (PEM or path).
- `key` (String, Sensitive) Client private key (PEM or path).
